text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government will need to find a further A$2 billion in savings in order to meet its commitment to balance Australia's Budget by 1998/99, following the release of figures that show the Government is facing a A$12.5 billion Budget blow-out over the next four years because of a fall in inflation and a large shortfall in company tax revenue. Page 1.

The overall employment level is predicted to decline, but a survey by the employment agency Drake International has found that those seeking accounting, legal and specialist outsourcing jobs will show the strongest level of employment growth. The constrution, IT and advertising sectors also expected to swell staff levels . The government and semi-government sectors however were planning to reduce their workforce. Page 2.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello firmly ruled out yesterday any plans to introduce a GST tax. He was responding to mounting pressure from business and welfare groups for tax reform which included this measure. Costello claims the GST is deeply unpopular with the Australian public, citing the Coalition's unsuccessful 1993 election campaign which figured a plan to introduce the GST prominently. Page 5.

With more than US$3 billion in Internet sales last year, it is predicted that online commerce will become a major activity of the corporate world next millennium. An international survey released yesterday by INC/LINK indicates consumers are increasingly buying online. The survey took a conservative view of Australian Internet usage, suggesting only 8.9 per cent of local households with PCs have access to the Internet. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has signalled another year of Budget cuts, as an embarrassing error on company tax - worth A$1.6 billion - helped add a further A$3 billion to the Budget deficit. Costello said the Government may need to introduce tax changes to ensure a balanced Budget is delivered in three years. Page 1.

As Federal Treasurer Peter Costello was forced yesterday to admit that his first Budget, delivered only five months ago, contained a serious error that will help open a A$3.5 billion a year hole in the revenue base by the next Federal election, he blamed the error on the Australian Tax Office and the Treasury Department. Page 1.

The Australian cricket team has reaffirmed its position as the best in the world with its second Test series win over the West Indies in 20 months. Australia won the series for the Frank Worrell trophy yesterday after defeating the tourists by an inningsand 183 runs in the fourth Test at Adelaide Oval. Page 1.

Government sources said last night Federal Cabinet is considering going back to honour its election promise to hold an elected people's convention for a republic this year. Details of the convention are expected to be released next week, as Cabinet yesteday voted against putting off the convention until 1998. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The release of the Federal Government's mid-year Budget review indicates new tax measures will need to be installed in the May Budget due to a A$3 billion blow-out in the deficit. The statement's revised economic forecasts show higher expectations for buiness investment than in the last Budget, and economic growth remains at 3.5 per cent. Page 1.

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello has admitted the Government will need to introduce new tax measures to get it through the current revenue crisis. His call reinforces the possible introduction of a goods and services tax, even though Costello reinforced the Government's commitment not to introduce such a tax this term. Page 1.

Aboriginal athletes Cathy Freeman and Kyle Vander-Kuyp yesterday took a tour around the troubled Sydney suburb of Redfern in an effort to bring out the better side of the area. The athletes were joined by the South Sydney rugby league team, led by Darrel Trindall, who grew up in the area. Page 1.

The Institute of Actuaries of Australia has warned the Federal Government there are 800 members a day leaving the private health insurance system, seeing it in danger of collapse. The Institute says the Government must drop its election commitment to equal premiums for all private health fund members regardless of risk or age. Page 1.
THE AGE

Treasury and Finance Department figures show a Budget blow-out of A$12.5 billion over the next four years, which may see Federal Treasurer Peter Costello need to launch another drive to cut the Budget deficit. A collapse in tax revenues has seen this yea's underlying Budget deficit, which was forecast at A$5.6 billion five months ago, tipped to reach A$8.5 billion. Page A1.

Victorian acting Agriculture Minister Bill McGrath has reassured dairy consumers that an outbreak of anthrax among northern Victorian cows would not threaten milk supplies. The death of cattle near Shepparton on Sunday alerted authorities of the outbreakof the disease, which is an infectious bacterial disease that can affect humans. Page A1.

Australian embassies and high commissions are registering a record number of students who want to come to Australia from Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, despite the intense coverage given by the local media to the race debate sparked by Independent Quensland MP Pauline Hanson. The diffusion of concerns is especially important for Victoria with 50 per cent of the estimated Malaysian students in Australia settling there. Page A1.

Six year old James Lewis is recovering in the Royal Children's Hospital after managing to attract attention to the overturned car which contained his mother, grandparents and two sisters. The car had fell 100 metres into a ravine off the Melba Highway nea Castella. James had climbed up the ravine and flagged down a passing motorist. Page A1.
